prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP Manifesto 2010: Empowering the People

Core purpose: Leave the EU to restore Britain’s three freedoms—action, resources, and people—reclaiming sovereignty, democracy and cash now handed to Brussels. UKIP argues the LibLabCon elite surrendered power, hid EU control, blocked a referendum, and burdened Britain with costly regulation and mass immigration. UKIP promises binding referenda, locally elected control, and national revival.

Economy and tax: Simplify and cut taxes—raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a single 31% flat tax merging Income Tax and Employees’ NI; phase out Employers’ NI; abolish Inheritance Tax when viable; replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax and return half of business rates to councils. Cut the state back to its 1997 size, scrap quangos and EU directives, and restore Bank of England control with a Glass–Steagall-style split and higher capital ratios.

Jobs and industry: Rebuild manufacturing with long-term programmes in defence, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport, and prison construction—creating around a million skilled jobs. Establish Production Enterprise Centres, denationalise universities/FE via student/training vouchers, toughen takeover rules for strategic sectors, and scrap costly green schemes that handicap competitiveness.

Immigration and asylum: End mass immigration with a five-year freeze and a future cap of about 50,000 annually. Leave the EU to control borders; use time-limited work permits and visas; criminalise overstaying; triple border staff; deport illegal migrants; no amnesty. Hold asylum seekers in secure centres, enforce first-safe-country rules, restore the Primary Purpose Rule, repeal the Human Rights Act and withdraw from the ECHR. End state promotion of multiculturalism in favour of a single, inclusive British civic culture.

Law and order: Put victims first. Elect County Police Boards, restore beat policing, scrap the Human Rights Act, ensure life means life, double prison places, end early release, adopt “three strikes,” withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant, introduce boot camps, and abolish the CPS for local prosecutions.

Defence: Increase spending by 40%; expand the Army by 25% and double the TA; restore naval strength with three carriers; boost RAF lift/helo fleets and JSF numbers; strengthen NATO ties, quit EU defence structures; maintain and replace Trident; cut MOD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

NHS and care: No frontline cuts; elect County Health Boards; scrap SHAs/PCTs; franchise services to drive efficiency while assets stay public; offer Health Credit Vouchers to opt out; restore matrons; bring back free eye tests and dental checks.

Education: School vouchers to expand parental choice; retain and expand grammar/professional schools with a broader merit test; raise teaching standards; end the 50% university target; restore grants via vouchers; elect County Education Boards; franchise schools; back home education; restore discipline.

Pensions and welfare: Create a universal, non-means-tested £130/week Citizen’s Pension; restore dividend tax credits; freeze unaffordable public-sector schemes; leave the EU pensions trap. Replace 70+ benefits with a flat-rate Basic Cash Benefit, let people work up to the allowance without penalty, enhance Child Benefit, introduce Nursery Vouchers, require residency, and expand workfare.

Trade and foreign affairs: Leave the political EU, keep free trade via a Swiss-style agreement, reclaim the UK’s WTO seat, build a Commonwealth Free Trade Area, pursue global deals, and champion democracy and self-determination.

Energy and environment: Climate-sceptic, cost-first approach. Provide up to 50% of electricity via nuclear; support clean coal; oppose uneconomic wind, keep any large schemes offshore; repeal the Climate Change Act; exit EU carbon schemes; convene a Royal Commission; electrify transport and invest in flood/coastal defences.

Transport: Invest £3bn more annually; improve roads; fair fuel duty mechanism; introduce a paid Britdisc for foreign lorries; build three high-speed rail lines; reopen lines; strengthen port links; back a Thames Estuary airport.

Housing and planning: Cut demand by controlling immigration; use empty homes; scrap regional quangos and the IPC; require binding local referenda on major schemes; protect Green Belt via elected conservators; end hidden development taxes; abolish HIPs; allow council bond issues; scrap empty property rates.

Constitution and governance: Direct Democracy—5% can trigger binding referenda; adopt AV+; elect Police, Health, and Education Boards and Mayors; replace devolved bodies with nation-specific Westminster MPs; English-only days; recall errant MPs; abolish regional government; back the monarchy and national institutions; repatriate powers from Brussels.

Culture and Britishness: Civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism and political correctness; protect iconic brands and weights/measures; teach Britain’s contributions; combat extremist Islam (burqa restrictions in public buildings, deport radical preachers, modern Treason Act); celebrate Commonwealth and English identity with new holidays.

Farming and fishing: Leave the CAP/CFP; phase subsidies sensibly; promote UK produce and animal welfare; allow producer co-ops; empower a supermarket ombudsman; county referenda on hunting; reclaim a 200-mile EEZ, end discards and industrial fishing, land all catch, and rebuild the fleet.

Other: Strong animal welfare; protect Royal Mail and Post Offices; permit designated smoking rooms; champion SMEs.
